claims.text: At stage-4 Notifications sends order emails to customerEmail in the order message, which the API copies from customers.email when it writes the outbox row; nothing updates customers.email from Keycloak.
data-ownership.md at stage-4 has one open question: the customer's email is held by the Keycloak account and customers.email, nothing keeps them equal, and the ADR 0014 pointer line is under it.
Keycloak stores per user whether the email is verified (emailVerified in a realm export/import file); every user in keycloak/donhang-realm.json at stage-4 has "emailVerified": true.
claims.source_hint: Keycloak 26.7 Server Administration Guide, user email verification; keycloak/donhang-realm.json @ stage-4 lines 68, 79, 90, 101, 112, 123

claims.text: The Customer class in DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs at stage-4 has Id, FullName, Email, City and IdentitySubject, and no field marking the email as verified.
threat-model.md records the unverified customers.email used for order emails as finding P3, to be fixed by ADR 0014.

ADR 0014's context section records that the access token the API receives already carries email and email_verified because client donhang-app has client scope email among its defaults (donhang-realm.json defaultClientScopes lists "email"), so the ADR needs no Keycloak change.

ADR 0014 decides: on placing an order the API reads email and email_verified from the checked access token and, if email_verified is true and email differs, updates customers.email in the same transaction as the order; unverified emails are not copied.
The outbox row is written in the same transaction as the order (stated as: one transaction stores the order, its outbox row and the refreshed customers.email).
claims.source_hint: ADR 0014 lines 38-39, 48-49; backend/messaging outbox lessons at stage-3

claims.text: Under ADR 0014 OrderMessage keeps its shape: customerEmail is still taken from customers when the outbox row is written, and Notifications and Payments do not change.

ADR 0014 weighs three options: keep both copies with a periodic sync job; Keycloak owns and the API refreshes customers.email from the token on each order; drop the copy and have Notifications ask Keycloak per email.

Options one and three each need a credential that can read every account at Keycloak (held by the job in one, by Notifications in three, widening its blast radius); three also makes each email depend on Keycloak. ADR rejects three for the credential, one also for keeping two owners.
ADR 0014 is accepted but not built at stage-4: no code refreshes the email, and the open question in data-ownership.md stays with a line pointing to the ADR.

ADR 0014's review conditions: emails that must reach customers who have not signed in for a long time, and another service needing a customer's email without that customer's access token; the copy is refreshed only on an order; its comments section at the end raises the refund-email case.

Refresh on use keeps customers.email current only up to the customer's last order; it adds no credential and no dependency on Keycloak to the email path, at the cost of a stale copy for customers who stop ordering. Option three has no stale copy but gives Notifications an every-account credential.

If a refund email must reach a customer who changed email and has not ordered since, keep the decision until it happens often enough to matter, then reopen the ADR and weigh asking Keycloak for that one customer's email, only when needed, against the credential it needs.
If a new service needs customers' emails without their access tokens, reopen the ADR before granting it a credential that reads every Keycloak account.
An ADR records a decision and its reasons; when the code follows can be planned separately, as ADR 0014 (accepted, not built at stage-4) shows.
